note: Project-local source inventory. The repository root evidence policy remains controlling; source class and operational states are separate. sources.title: Critical-edition introduction, 'Ds. Jodocus van Lodenstein en zijn Uyt-spanningen 1676', pp. 645-647
sources.type: Modern scholarly introduction in the copyrighted 2005 edition
supports: In December 1673 Lodenstein was held as a hostage of the French, far from Utrecht
He sent songs to the Utrecht circle, printed in 1674 as 'Meditatiën over eenige van Gods eygenschappen'
Many songs were written for singing in the Utrecht circle; melodies were drawn partly from popular 16th/17th-century tunes and partly from unidentified contemporary compositions
limits: Copyrighted secondary literature: paraphrase only, never quotation.
Describes the corpus generally; it does not date any individual poem.

Printed reading '4. in Loumaand 1674' for II

Copyrighted selection and annotation: cite, do not reproduce.

sources.title: Etymologiebank — stikken (Van Veen/Van der Sijs 1997; De Vries 1971)
sources.type: Etymological dictionary entry, freely readable
supports: That 'stikken' in the sense of smothering is historically one word with 'stikken' (to stitch), an intensivum of 'steken', glossed as 'blijven steken, niet verder kunnen'
That the sense required by Lodenstein's rhyme with 'verquickt' is the 'stuck fast, choked' sense rather than simple adhesion
limits: An etymological dictionary answers a historical question, not a synchronic one: it cannot tell us what the 1676 reader understood by the line.
De Vries and Van Veen/Van der Sijs are secondary authorities; the WNT remains the primary tool.
